title: Constant and linear coordinates on the first-order power-series quotient
statement: Let K be a field, sigma a finite set, T=K[[X_i : i in sigma]] [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], and N the ideal generated by all X_i. There exists a ring isomorphism e:T/N^2 -> K plus K^sigma, the trivial square-zero extension [def-sc-trivial-square-zero-extension], with q in the image of N if and only if the first coordinate of e(q) is zero. The assertion includes the empty variable set.

source.place: Tag 07EI, construction of f_1; coefficient field from Algebra Tag 032A

proof.text: Define jet(f)=(constantCoeff(f),(coeff_(e_i)(f))_i). The degree-one Cauchy product is coeff_(e_i)(fg)=constantCoeff(f) coeff_(e_i)(g)+constantCoeff(g) coeff_(e_i)(f). Together with constant coefficient multiplicativity, this proves jet is a ring map to the trivial square-zero extension. The Lean proof obtains the same identity from the formal derivative Leibniz rule at exponent zero.

The variables ideal N has zero constant coefficient. Products of two elements of N therefore map to zero under jet, so N^2 lies in the kernel. Conversely any element of the kernel has zero constant and linear coefficients, so lies in N^2.

Every pair (c,v) is the jet of normal(c,v)=C(c)+sum_i C(v_i)X_i. Hence the induced map T/N^2 -> K plus K^sigma is surjective, and its kernel is zero by the previous step. It is the required ring isomorphism.

An element of the image of N has zero constant coordinate. Conversely if e(q) has zero first coordinate, normal(e(q)) is a finite sum of multiples of X_i and belongs to N. Its quotient class equals q by injectivity of e, proving the ideal membership equivalence.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_firstOrder_coordinates (σ : Type u) [Finite σ] (K : Type v) [Field K] :
    let T := MvPowerSeries σ K
    let N : Ideal T := Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i ↦ (X i : T)))
    ∃ e : (T ⧸ N ^ 2) ≃+* TrivSqZeroExt K (σ → K),
      ∀ q : T ⧸ N ^ 2, q ∈ N.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (N ^ 2)) ↔ (e q).fst = 0
